text: Cross-snapshot range defect: x1 and x2 are computed once from the lengths of snapshot 0100 on lines 14-15, but z1 and z2 are replaced by snapshots 0200/0300/0400 on lines 45-46, 56-57, and 66-67 without recomputing coordinates. Any later snapshot length change causes plot dimension errors or assigns coordinates from the wrong grid extent.

The positive-V F4 diffusion branch uses H(I,J+1)+H(I,J) while its concentration difference and face velocity are on the south face J-1; the negative branch uses H(I,J-1)+H(I,J). This sign-dependent geometry mismatch changes diffusion solely with flow direction.
review_note: Codex deep re-audit 2026-08-28: The positive-flow south-face diffusion uses the north-cell depth pair, while the negative branch uses the south-face pair. F4 feeds the concentration update and no guard or zero factor removes this sign-dependent geometry error.

text: For px==1, the x wall block's IF(npx==0) ... ELSEIF(npx==px-1) executes only the west condition and skips the east condition. The y block has an explicit py==1 case setting both sides, confirming the x single-partition omission.
review_note: Codex deep re-audit 2026-08-28: With px=1, npx is both 0 and px-1, so ELSEIF makes the east-wall F1 assignment unreachable. The analogous py=1 branch explicitly handles both ends, and no later x-boundary assignment neutralizes the omission.

text: Both deposition implementations evaluate (1-n_porosity)/CH before multiplication by CH, with no CH>0 guard. Active wet cells can have CH=0 initially or after MAX clamping in sediment_solver, so division by zero precedes any algebraic cancellation.
review_note: MIN cap absorbs Inf before *CH; IEEE-benign

text: sediment_flux forms HxL/HxR (Mloc1 by Nloc) and HyL/HyR (Mloc by Nloc1) by adding whole Zb, whose cell-centered shape is Mloc by Nloc. No face reconstruction or slice is applied to Zb, producing shape/interface inconsistency or wrong bed placement at faces.
review_note: Codex deep re-audit 2026-08-28: Cell-centered Zb(Mloc,Nloc) is added as a whole array to x- and y-face arrays whose respective extents are Mloc1 and Nloc1. The intrinsic assignments require conforming shapes; there is no reconstruction, slice, or guard to make them conform.

text: Both loops at L14-L33 use length(n4) while indexing n5 through n10; shorter arrays fail and longer arrays retain unshifted or untouched tail rows.

If eta(:,1) or WGdata(:,2) contains NaN, max at lines 17 or 25 can be NaN and equality is false for every iteration; empty inputs also skip the loops. num_t_shift and/or exp_t_shift are then used before assignment at line 32.

Measured plotting at lines 43 and 62 uses length(veldata) as a row bound. Because MATLAB length returns the largest dimension, a file with fewer rows than columns indexes beyond its row range; size(veldata,1) is the required interface dimension.

relative_error is assigned without a k subscript at line 46 inside the 11-iteration loop on lines 41-47, so every iteration overwrites the preceding result and only the k=11 value survives; this is inconsistent with the indexed std_data and std_model outputs on lines 44-45.

Cross-file length/time mismatch: every station read overwrites the shared time vector and scalar Ndata (for example east lines 84-90 and west lines 112-118). The later global loop DO K=1,Ndata at line 183 therefore uses only the last-read station's length and time base for every side and station; if files differ, earlier shorter arrays are read uninitialized or earlier longer samples are silently truncated, and differing timestamps are never compared.
review_note: Codex deep re-audit 2026-08-28: convert.f assumes a common record count and clock, but the native producer advances every active station buffer in the same station-output call and stores the same global TIME. Differing native station lengths/timestamps require truncated or externally altered files, not a reachable normal producer path.

text: Out-of-bounds search: lines 251-254 increment Kstart while TIME(Kstart)<time_cut without checking Kstart<=Ndata (or Ntotal). If time_cut exceeds the final available timestamp, TIME is indexed beyond valid data and potentially beyond its allocation before the loop can terminate.
Both L14-L33 loops use length(n4) while indexing n5..n10; unequal station lengths cause out-of-range access for shorter files or leave longer tails unprocessed.
Use-before-supplied interface defect across L161 and L179: the no-argument branch is guarded by nargin<1, so a legal one-argument call enters the else branch and references missing filename2 at L179.

Definite zero-index failure in both peak searches: kk and kk2 start at 0 on lines 16 and 28, while loops begin at element 2 and update only for a strictly larger later value. If the first element is maximal (or either series has length 1), kk/kk2 remains 0 and lines 25/37 perform illegal MATLAB index-0 access. They must begin at 1 for the initialization from element 1 to be coherent.

Range coupling: both loops use length(n4) as the bound (lines 14 and 25) while indexing n5 through n10 on lines 16-21 and 27-32; any shorter station array causes out-of-range indexing, and extra rows in longer arrays are left untransformed.

Halo-exchange interface gap across L324-L325,L365-L414,L781: EXCHANGE sends staggered P/Q through PHI_COLL_VARIABLE_LENGTH, but that routine only reflects physical-edge ghosts and returns without any MPI/phi_exch call; ordinary PHI_COLL always finishes with phi_exch. Unless another caller-owned exchange exists, P/Q internal-processor halos remain stale when these fields are enabled.
review_note: Codex deep re-audit 2026-08-28: The only scheme that consumes P/Q as exchanged cell-interface state is hard-disabled by PQ_scheme=.FALSE.; the active scheme uses locally formed HU/HV fluxes. Thus the absent P/Q MPI exchange does not affect computed output in the in-tree configuration.

text: Periodic overwrite defect across L445-L504 and L664-L779: PHI_COLL fills periodic y ghosts first, and VTYPE 1/2/3 protect later y boundary logic with .NOT.PERIODIC (e.g. L643), but VTYPE 4/5/6 south/north blocks have no such guard. On periodic end ranks they can overwrite periodic data with zero, symmetric, or antisymmetric physical-boundary values before phi_exch.
review_note: Codex deep re-audit 2026-08-28: All in-tree PHI_COLL callers select VTYPE 1, 2, or 3, whose y-boundary blocks have the periodic guard. No caller selects the unguarded VTYPE 4-6 branches, so the proposed overwrite is unreachable.

text: AGE is declared INTENT(OUT) at L110, but its incoming values are read in the initiation/aging test at L141-L146 and as neighbor history at L175-L214, before every element is necessarily defined by this invocation. The algorithm requires persistent prior age, so the declared interface conflicts with its use and should be assessed as INOUT.
Both length-based loops at L39-L57 use length(n4) while indexing n5 through n10; unequal station lengths can either index past shorter inputs or leave tails of longer inputs untransformed.

PHI_COLL_OUTER_GPU duplicates hundreds of lines of PHI_COLL_GPU reflection logic but omits its final communication call. The duplication makes later parity/boundary fixes prone to diverge and is the direct source of the internal-halo inconsistency above.
review_note: Codex deep re-audit 2026-08-28: PHI_COLL_OUTER_GPU is used for physical-edge reflection only; moment_gpu explicitly recomputes the derivative halo through two ghost layers from already available base-field halos. Non-root/internal ranks therefore do not consume an unsynchronized derivative halo from this routine.

text: Use-before-supplied interface defect across L166 and L184: a one-argument call enters the else branch and evaluates isempty(filename2) even though filename2 was not supplied.

Use-before-assignment across conditionals occurs in every Cartesian/ZALPHA reconstruction family. U4xL/U4xR and V4xL/V4xR are produced only inside IF(DISPERSION) near L428-L433, L803-L808, and L1305-L1310, but PL/PR/Fx/Gx consume them unconditionally immediately afterward. The same pattern affects U4y/V4y and QL/QR/Gy/Fy. With DISPERSION false, stale or undefined reconstructed arrays enter fluxes rather than the nondispersive formulas used by the nested non-ZALPHA branch.

Use-before-assignment across branches: breaking_kernel assigns DXg and DYg only inside the Age_sh<=ZERO, non-immediate-trigger branch at L168-L184, but all paths then use them to compute xmk/ymk at L234-L238. If the immediate trigger branch L162-L164 or positive-age branch L166-L167 is taken, wavemaker footprint selection consumes undefined DXg/DYg.
